+#### Custom Function Rules
+
+Custom functions must satisfy the following requirements:
+
+- **Function names must be in camelCase notation.** For example, `myFunction` is a valid name, while `my_function` and `myfunction` are not.
+- **All function arguments are passed to a function as a single `params` array parameter.** The function receives all arguments in the `params` array no matter how many arguments the corresponding call in an expression has. To access a required argument, use its index in the `params` array.
+
+The code sample below demonstrates the correct function signature for a function that takes two arguments:
+
+```javascript
+function myFunction(params) {
+  // All function arguments are available in the params array
+  var firstArgument = params[0];
+  var secondArgument = params[1];
+  return firstArgument + secondArgument;
+}
+```
+
+A function that declares arguments as separate parameters, as regular JavaScript functions do, is incorrect:
+
+```javascript
+// Incorrect
+function myFunction(firstArgument, secondArgument) {
+  return firstArgument + secondArgument;
+}
+```

## What I did

After inspecting the actual rendering code, the only React component handling multiple-text questions is `src/react/reactquestionmultipletext.tsx`. Its row (`<tr>`), label cells, and value cells were keyed, but the two dynamically created cells per item used **index keys** (`"label" + i`, `"value" + i`). When items are added, removed, or reordered, those index keys shift, so React can no longer correctly reconcile the dynamically created spans/elements (mismatched text-input state, re-rendering warnings from unstable keys).

I changed the cell keys to use the stable, unique per-item identifier (`item.editor.id`), matching the Vue implementation (`src/vue/multipletext.vue`) which keys on `item.editor.id`:

- `<td key={"label" + item.editor.id}>`
- `<SurveyQuestionAndErrorsCell key={"value" + item.editor.id}>`

Verification:
- `Question.id` is a stable unique string (`src/question.ts:73`, `709`), so keys are unique among siblings and stable across re-renders.
- Change is behavior-preserving (DOM structure unchanged) and fixes the reconciliation hazard for multiple-text questions.
- Only this one file changed for this task; all prior accepted work (Welsh, Japanese pagePrevText, header fix, calculated-values fix, docs, TestCafe typo fixes) remains intact.

No runtime tests were run (node_modules unavailable, per constraints); only static review and the type compatibility check were performed.
